title: No way to bulk-reorder or persist a score sort (queue reorder is one move at a time)
findings_note: dogfooding re-sort: reordering the queue needs one 'move --to' per item; list --sort score is view-only. Consider 'slicer sort --by score' to persist, or move accepting a full order / multiple ids.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Reordering the queue is one `slicer move` per item, and `list --sort score` is view-only, so
re-sorting the whole roadmap by priority means N manual moves. Filed dogfooding a re-prioritize
that took 17 moves.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- src/slicer/ops.py: `sort_queue` reorders the queue by effective score.
- src/slicer/cli.py: `slicer sort [--by score]`.
- tests; README, getting-started, agents docs.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add `slicer sort [--by score]` that reorders the whole queue by effective score (descending,
stable) in one command, persisting exactly the `list --sort score` view. It overwrites the
manual `move` order with priority order, records one `sort` log entry, and is idempotent (a
no-op sort writes nothing).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
After scrambling with `move`, `slicer sort` makes `list` order equal `list --sort score`; a
second `sort` reports nothing moved. Focused sort tests, the unit suite, slicer check, and git
diff --check.
